newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch cocoa trade repeats call for bulk contract.
newsitem.headline: Dutch cocoa trade repeats call for bulk contract.

text.p: The Dutch Cocoa Association (NCV) has repeated its call for the cocoa futures markets in London and New York to establish a contract compatible with the growing trend towards bulk shipment.
In its annual review of 1996, published this week, the NCV said bulk cocoa was now a "fact of life" and both exchanges needed to recognise this for the benefit of all traders.
"Opening up the possibility to tender bulk cocoa on the futures markets will improve the market's liquidity and decrease possibilities of price manipulations," it said.
The NCV noted that LIFFE, which took over the former London Commodity Exchange, had set up a working group to study proposals for a new contract.

The report described 1996 as a "breakthrough" year for the transport of cocoa in bulk, and estimates that some 60 percent of the cocoa destined for processing in Amsterdam was delivered to the port under bulk conditions.
But there were problems -- the decline in bag handling at the port would have negative implications for employment there and the receiving industry had to improve its quality controls.
"This creates a new field of activity for the warehousing companies, which have already set up their own companies in harbours at origin to exercise their quality controlling tasks," it said.
Amsterdam remained the world's largest receiving port for cocoa, and had extended this leading position in 1996.
